ADU218 K0 closed-contact resistance characterisation
====================================================
Witness: SDM4065A s/n SDM46A0CA00021 fw 0.0.0.20
Question: the datasheet gives 700 mohm typical / 1.1 ohm maximum
on-state resistance for the ADU218's Panasonic AQZ207 PhotoMOS
relays. The bench measures roughly nine times that. Is the extra
resistance in the relay, in the leads, or in the measurement?

K0 closed (RPK0=1)

--- 2-wire, eight repeats (establishes the noise floor) ---
  0: 6.13937 ohm
  1: 6.13964 ohm
  2: 6.13984 ohm
  3: 6.14020 ohm
  4: 6.13987 ohm
  5: 6.14014 ohm
  6: 6.13996 ohm
  7: 6.14035 ohm
  mean=6.13992 ohm  spread=0.983 mohm
  -> the spread is milliohms, so the offset is systematic, not noise

--- 4-wire (would remove lead resistance IF sense leads present) ---
  4-wire: -146172.31500 ohm
  delta 2w-4w = 146178.45492 ohm
  NOTE: with no sense leads attached this function returns a
  plausible-looking negative number rather than raising. Do not
  use 4-wire as a witness on this setup (KNOWN_LIMITATIONS H-5).

--- continuity function ---
  continuity: 6.00636 ohm

--- open state: is 'OPEN' truly out of range? ---
K0 open (RPK0=0)
  SDM4065AOverloadError: 9.9E37 overload sentinel (over-range)

--- DC voltage across the open contact ---
  DCV: 0.000595 V

CONCLUSION: unexplained. The milliohm spread rules out noise.
(This paragraph originally cited KNOWN_LIMITATIONS H-5's ~79 mohm
as an upper bound on the series error, which was a mistake of the
same kind as the datasheet comparison below: H-5's figure was
measured on a QR10x 100 ohm setpoint with a different lead set and
different connections, so it bounds THAT path, not this one. It
also turned out to be wrong by 57x for this path -- see the
RESOLVED section at the end of this file. H-5's own datasheet
bound is 0.2 ohm, still far below the excess.) Candidates not yet
separated: the specific relay's actual
on-resistance, contact/clip resistance at the terminal block, or
a range-dependent offset in the 2-wire function. Recorded as open
rather than rationalised. The driver must NOT use the datasheet
on-resistance as a validation threshold.

FOLLOW-UP: the part datasheet was read, and the comparison this
file makes is not valid
------------------------------------------------------------------
The "700 mohm typical / 1.1 ohm maximum" in the question above is
quoted from Ontrak's ADU218 manual, which reprints it with NO test
conditions. Panasonic's own catalogue for the part (ASCTB467E,
PhotoMOS Power SIL 1 Form A; the AQZ207 has no standalone
datasheet) states them explicitly in a Condition column:

    IF = 10 mA        LED forward current
    IL = Max.         load current AT MAXIMUM = 1.0 A for AQZ207
    Within 1 s        take the reading within 1 s (thermal bound)

So 1.1 ohm is a short-pulse figure at ONE AMP. Every reading in
this file was taken with the DMM's ohmmeter sourcing on the order
of 1 mA -- about three orders of magnitude below the specified
condition, and with indefinite dwell rather than a 1 s pulse.

Therefore: 6.14 ohm neither violates nor satisfies the datasheet
maximum. There is no applicable limit at this test current. This
unit must NOT be recorded as out of spec on the strength of this
file.

It is also still not explained. The natural story -- PhotoMOS R_on
rising steeply as load current falls -- is NOT supported by the
datasheet: it contains no R_on-vs-load-current curve at all (R_on
is plotted only against ambient temperature), and its single
lower-current data point runs the other way. Graph 3-4 is taken at
0.4 A and reads about 0.65 ohm at 25 C, slightly BELOW the 0.7 ohm
typical quoted at 1.0 A. The output I-V curve (graph 9-2) is a
straight line through the origin with no knee, but at +/-4 A full
scale it cannot resolve 1 mA either way. Temperature is the only
R_on modifier the datasheet quantifies and it bounds that at about
1.5x from 25 C to 85 C. 5.44 ohm remains unaccounted for.

One candidate is now closed: the AC/DC variants really are two
MOSFETs in anti-series (Panasonic's schematic, and visible in the
~2x R_on ratio against each DC-only sibling: AQZ107 0.34 ohm ->
AQZ207 0.7 ohm). But that doubling is ALREADY inside the published
0.7 ohm. It must not be applied a second time.

CORRECTION to this file's own method, while here: the eight
repeats above are 2-WIRE. The 4-wire attempt is the line that
returned -146172 ohm because no sense leads were attached. Any
later summary of this measurement should say 2-wire. And 2-wire
does include lead and terminal-block contact resistance, which a
4-wire reading would have excluded -- which, per the RESOLVED
section below, is where the excess turned out to live. (This
paragraph also leaned on the ~79 mohm bound to argue the
distinction did not matter. It did matter, and the bound did not
apply; see the note in the CONCLUSION above.)

The discriminating experiment is a measurement at the datasheet's
own condition: 1.0 A, expecting <= 1.1 ohm, or 0.4 A for direct
comparison against graph 3-4's ~0.65 ohm. That energises a
120 V-rated relay into a real load, so it is an operator decision
and is deliberately not scripted here.

RESOLVED: the excess is not in the relay
-----------------------------------------
This file's CONCLUSION above lists three candidates and declines to
choose. A later session chose for it, by accident. See
on_resistance_drift.txt for the data; the short version:

The same closed contact read 10.694 ohm, with nothing in software
changed -- a +4.55 ohm step from the 6.13992 ohm mean here. The value
is milliohm-stable on BOTH sides of that step: 3.93 mohm across ten
re-actuations (vs 0.12-2.35 mohm within a single close), and 1.67 mohm
of drift over a 28 s hold. So each side of the step is a good
measurement of something; they are measurements of different things.

Against the three candidates listed at lines 43-45:

  "the specific relay's actual on-resistance"  ELIMINATED. A
    semiconductor's R_on does not step 74% between sessions and then
    hold to 4 mohm over ten actuations. The datasheet quantifies only
    temperature as an R_on modifier, bounded ~1.5x over 25-85 C.

  "a range-dependent offset in the 2-wire function"  ELIMINATED
    independently, in latency_after_command.txt section B: pinned
    200 ohm vs autoranged differ by 1.353 mohm against a 4550 mohm
    step. That measurement also supplies what this file failed to
    record -- the DMM's range and autorange state, which cannot be
    recovered from a transcript after the fact.

  "contact/clip resistance at the terminal block"  the only candidate
    that predicts a step-then-hold. Confirmed by elimination.

So the ~5 ohm this file recorded as unexplained is attributed, and the
answer is that it was never the relay. Which specific connection moved
is not identifiable from the host: the DMM leads, the K0 screw
terminals and the clip joints are in series and all outside the part.
This is not an accusation that anyone disturbed anything -- it is
evidence a series connection differs between sessions, and the cause
is outside what a script can see. Ask the operator.

CONFIRMED BY THE OPERATOR (asked, not assumed): the probes were
re-seated between the two sessions, deliberately, to improve
connection stability -- and left untouched for the two hours spanning
the drift and re-actuation captures. That is the right element, the
right interval, and the right quiet window, so the elimination above
is a confirmed cause rather than a surviving candidate.

Note the direction: re-seating the probes made the reading HIGHER,
6.14 -> 10.69 ohm. And note what the probes actually are -- clamped
into a screw terminal, so the contact point quality is not guaranteed
by construction. The operator's stated improvement is MECHANICAL (the
probe moves less than it did), which is a different quantity from
electrical contact resistance and does not bound it.

A claim made here in an earlier pass -- that the new joint is "both
more stable and more resistive" -- was withdrawn: it compared this
session's ACROSS-close spread (3.93 mohm) with the earlier session's
WITHIN-close spread (0.983 mohm), which are different quantities. The
only like-for-like pair is within-close, 0.983 mohm before against
0.12-2.35 mohm after: comparable, arguably slightly worse, and no
across-close data exists from the earlier session at all. The
comparison cannot be made in either direction.

What stands is that the reading is stable IN ABSOLUTE TERMS over the
measured window, which is all the elimination argument needed, and that
it went up by 4.55 ohm. So repeat precision is no evidence a figure
describes the relay: this one is milliohm-repeatable and measures a
screw clamp.

Which also means the 6.14 ohm mean at the top of this file was never a
relay measurement either. Both numbers are probe-path resistance. This
file's original question -- "is the extra resistance in the relay, in
the leads, or in the measurement?" -- is answered: the leads, in every
session, including the one that produced the eight repeats above.

The driver consequence at line 46-47 stands and is now permanent rather
than provisional. It used to rest on "the number is unexplained," which
a later explanation could have dissolved. It now rests on something that
does not expire: this measurement is dominated by series connections the
driver cannot see or know about, so any figure it reported would be a
property of the bench wiring wearing a relay's name.
